role.altitude: The sports official keeps timing play, starting and stopping, directing competitors, watching teams and deciding how to handle a match; copying times onto sheets, walking for start list changes and mailing colleagues for old match reports shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working from digital start lists and timing exports
Using federation match records for preparation
role.ambitious_version: An official who arrives prepared from the federation's own records, with eyes free for the play.

tasks.short: Check timing equipment, keep track of event times including elapsed time during game segments, start or stop play, time finishes, write times on the sheet, enter them for results and report irregularities.

steps.what: Official checks the timing equipment before the event
Official tracks elapsed time during game segments and starts or stops play when necessary
Official watches the finish and stops the watch for each competitor's race times
Official writes the times on the paper timing sheet
Official enters times from the sheet into the results system
Official reports timing irregularities to the referee

tasks.design: At events with electronic timing, the timing system records each finish time, and the official confirms them on a tablet instead of writing them on a paper sheet. The official still watches the finish and keeps a backup watch. Keeping game time, starting and stopping play and reporting irregularities stay with the official.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times were written on paper sheets at the finish.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic timing that exports finish times.
tasks.human_edge: Stopping play at the right moment for an injured player.

evidence.claim: A federation's digital match form lets the referee enter the result directly.
Electronic timing records finish times and exports them.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping event times; starting races (task 3914) and compiling scores and records (task 3923) are sibling tasks.
s5 is part of compiling scores and records, which sibling task 3923 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s4: electronic timing at about 70% of events; s4 is priced at that share.
Timing play, the finish watch and reporting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of events with electronic timing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: club events with hand timing; high: events with electronic timing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the start list, fetch late changes, call participants and direct them to assigned areas such as starting blocks or penalty areas, check their positions and handle late or missing participants.

steps.what: Official checks the start list for heat and lane assignments
Official walks to the secretariat to collect late changes to the start list
Official calls participants and directs them to assigned areas, such as starting blocks or penalty areas
Official checks that each participant is in the right place
Official handles late or missing participants with the referee

tasks.design: The start list lives in the competition system, and late changes such as withdrawals and lane swaps appear on the official's tablet, instead of the official walking to the secretariat for them. Calling, directing and checking participants and handling late arrivals stay with the official.
tasks.previous_blocker: Late changes were fetched on foot from the secretariat.
tasks.enabler_now: Competition systems that push start list changes to tablets.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a nervous young athlete at the blocks.

reach.learn: Whether fewer officials come to the desk.

evidence.claim: Competition systems can push start list changes to officials' devices.

assumptions: Boundary: directing participants to areas; verifying credentials and starting order (task 3922) and starting races (task 3914) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: digital start lists with pushed changes at about 60% of events; s2 is priced at that share.
s2 saves the walk to the secretariat.
Calling, directing and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of late changes per event.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few late changes; high: large meets with many changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask colleagues for earlier match reports, read reports and disciplinary records, watch the teams, keep notes, discuss with fellow officials and decide what to anticipate to research and study players and teams.

steps.what: Official asks colleagues by mail for earlier match reports on the teams
Official reads earlier match reports and disciplinary records of players and teams
Official watches the teams play live or on video
Official keeps own notes on team tactics and player behaviour
Official discusses the match with assistant referees beforehand
Official decides which issues to anticipate in future engagements and how to handle them

tasks.design: The federation's match system shows, for each team in the official's next match, earlier match reports, cards and incidents in one view, instead of the official mailing colleagues for reports and reading them one by one. Watching the teams, keeping notes, briefing assistants and deciding what to anticipate stay with the official. Nothing scores or ranks players, and no health information is shown.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier reports were gathered by mail from colleagues.
tasks.enabler_now: Federation match systems with reports and cards per team.
tasks.still_hard: Lower leagues with few digital reports.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing which rivalry will flare up in the second half.

evidence.claim: A federation's digital match form lets the referee enter the result directly.
Injury notes are health data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: studying players and teams; officiating (task 3909) and reporting to regulating organisations (task 3918) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: match reports and cards recorded in the federation system for about 70% of matches; s1 is priced at that share.
s1 saves the mail round to colleagues; s2 saves opening reports one by one.
Access to reports is limited to appointed officials, and the view holds no health data.
Watching, notes, briefing and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of leagues with digital match reports.
research_questions: Do officials report fewer surprises in matches?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: lower leagues; high: leagues with full digital reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
